coverage_summary: Reviewed all trajectories, documented transformations, ports, lifecycle phases, model contexts, and opaque boundaries. Several graph dependencies and documented routes are missing or unsupported.

findings.detail: Cell-description construction is represented as a custom opaque operation even though the catalog already provides `serialize`, whose interface matches merging metadata and free text into an ordered textual payload.

evidence.quote: We construct textual descriptions of cells by merging the free-form cell explanations and the cell metadata from CellxGenes.

findings.required_change: Use the existing `serialize` operation with unspecified template/order details, preserving the documented uncertainty.

findings.detail: The graph invents `llama_decoder_input` as an output of an undocumented token-to-decoder transformation. The paper documents tokenization and use of a decoder-only LLaMA model, but does not establish this intermediate representation.

evidence.quote: We tokenize the textual description of cells into a sequence of tokens t ( i ) = [ t ( i ) 1 , t ( i ) 2 , . . . , t ( i ) T ] using the tokenizer in text LLM.
For the text LLM, we utilize LLaMA-2 7B [47], a decoder-only transformer that excels at text generation.

findings.required_change: Bind `text_tokens` directly to the LLaMA receiving boundary, or retain an opaque decoder boundary without asserting a separate decoder-input node.

findings.detail: The negative-sample selection receives only one paired text description, although the paper says two negative samples are selected for each sample. A single description cannot establish the negative-sample candidate pool.

evidence.quote: We select 2 negative samples for each sample to calculate the InfoNCE [74] loss.

findings.required_change: Add an explicitly represented candidate/batch text pool, or keep negative-sample construction opaque without binding the single paired description as its source.

findings.detail: The Q-Former initialization from BiomedBERT is omitted from the Stage 1 projector state and all inherited Q-Former contexts.

evidence.quote: We initialize the Q-Former with weights from BiomedBERT [48], a BERT encoder trained on PubMed abstracts and biomedical literature [49].

findings.required_change: Record BiomedBERT initialization separately from the Stage 1 update state and carry it into the inherited Stage 2/downstream Q-Former context.

findings.detail: The Stage 1 cell-encoder route directly consumes a normalized full-gene vector but does not connect the documented top-value selection and padding before scGPT input.

evidence.quote: To mitigate data sparsity, we retain the top 2,048 most expressed genes per cell, which captures the majority of meaningful signals.
For cellular input representation, we implement a top-value alignment strategy that selects the 2,048 highest-expressed genes along with their expression values.

findings.required_change: Add the documented top-value alignment/padding path to the Stage 1 scGPT input, or explicitly identify `stage1_normalized_cell` as the already-prepared output of that path with supporting evidence.

findings.detail: The Stage 2 cell-to-text route directly feeds an expression input to the scLLM while omitting the documented model-input preparation of normalization, top-value alignment, and padding.

evidence.quote: Since absolute gene expression values can vary across measurement platforms, we apply row-wise normalization before feeding into the model:
For cellular input representation, we implement a top-value alignment strategy that selects the 2,048 highest-expressed genes along with their expression values.

findings.required_change: Connect the Stage 2 cell input to the documented scGPT preprocessing path or mark the input as a model-ready prepared representation with complete evidence.

findings.detail: The zero-shot annotation route feeds a generic expression vector directly to scLLM and omits the documented preprocessing required for cellular input.

evidence.quote: Since absolute gene expression values can vary across measurement platforms, we apply row-wise normalization before feeding into the model:
For cellular input representation, we implement a top-value alignment strategy that selects the 2,048 highest-expressed genes along with their expression values.

findings.required_change: Add or explicitly reference normalization, top-value selection, and padding before the zero-shot scLLM encoder.

findings.detail: The annotation selection is decomposed into `rank` followed by `select`, asserting an ordering the paper does not state. The paper only documents choosing the class with the minimum combined loss.

evidence.quote: select the class that minimizes the combined loss λ L InfoNCE +(1 -λ ) L CE as prediction.

findings.required_change: Use a single minimum-loss selection boundary, or leave the selection operation opaque; remove the unsupported rank-then-select sequence.

findings.detail: `annotation_candidate_text_features` is declared but never produced or consumed. The comparison step instead binds raw candidate descriptions, leaving the documented text-representation dependency disconnected.

evidence.quote: Similarly, for a textual description represented by the token sequence t ( i ) = { t 1 , . . . , t L } , we extract the text embedding via the BERT module within the Q-Former as h text = BERT ( t ( i ) ) .
Given a cell x ( i ) , we calculate its contrastive and matching losses against textual descriptions { t j } of all possible cell types

findings.required_change: Either add an opaque candidate-text encoding boundary producing `annotation_candidate_text_features` and bind it to comparison, or remove the dangling feature node and state that encoding is internal to the comparison boundary.

findings.detail: The fine-tuning annotation projector omits the Q-Former query side input despite claiming the same inference approach as zero-shot annotation. The documented Q-Former uses 32 learnable queries.

evidence.quote: In the fine-tuning scenario, we continue training scMMGPT on the downstream dataset using the alignment loss L align, and employ the same inference approach as in the zero-shot case.
The cell-to-text projector is implemented with a Query Transformer (Q-Former) [33] with 32 learnable queries

findings.required_change: Add a trajectory-specific Q-Former query resource or explicitly reuse the pretrained query parameter, and bind it to the projection boundary.

findings.detail: The clustering route directly feeds generic cell profiles to scGPT without representing the documented model-input preparation.

For cellular input representation, we implement a top-value alignment strategy that selects the 2,048 highest-expressed genes along with their expression values.
given a set of cells { x ( i ) } , we obtain their representations as c ( i ) = scGPT ( x ( i ) )

findings.required_change: Add or explicitly reference normalization, top-value alignment, and padding before zero-shot scGPT feature extraction.

findings.detail: The cell-description generation fine-tuning route also feeds an unprepared expression vector directly to the frozen scLLM, omitting the documented scGPT input preparation.

evidence.quote: Since absolute gene expression values can vary across measurement platforms, we apply row-wise normalization before feeding into the model:
For cellular input representation, we implement a top-value alignment strategy that selects the 2,048 highest-expressed genes along with their expression values.
For cell description generation tasks, we further fine-tune the text LLM with the cell-to-text translation loss L c2t, while freezing both the scLLM and the Q-former.

findings.required_change: Add or explicitly reference the shared scGPT preprocessing path before the frozen scLLM encoder.

findings.detail: The paper reports text-conditioned pseudo-cell generation as an evaluated task, but the assembly contains only the Stage 2 training route and no downstream/inference trajectory for this task.

evidence.quote: We conduct cell generation experiments on the immune tissue [60] dataset.
Text → Cell Generation: In the reverse direction, we enable the generation of cell embeddings conditioned on textual input.

findings.required_change: Add a text-conditioned pseudo-cell generation task/phase trajectory, or explicitly designate the existing text-to-cell route as serving both Stage 2 training and downstream generation inference.
